thread:
Devon: Heads-up: canary for the 70B convo route spiked in p99 this morning after the kernel selector tweak. p50/p95 unchanged, tails bad.
Irene: Which kernel transition did the selector choose? any change aten->custom or fused->fallback?
AJ: I caught a similar pattern on staging during the overnight perf sweep. Only the tail worsened, not median.
Devon: Looks like it's tied to KV cache misses. When requests hit a cold KV shard we fall back to an unoptimized codegen and that path queues behind big batches.
Sneh: Do we have KV churn metrics? eviction churn could amplify cold-miss rate.
Devon: Logs show a cluster of `kv_fetch` timeouts aligned with the p99 windows.
Liam: Can you share the condensed profiler trace you ran? want to see whether it's PCIe copies, kernel launch stalls, or pure compute.
Devon: pasted a short trace snippet from the spot run:

```
# profiler excerpt
time_ms | op        | kernel_path  | gpu_util
-------------------------------------------
0.7     | kv_lookup  | cached       | 70%
4.8     | kv_miss    | fallback     | 90%  <-- long tail
1.2     | attn_fwd   | fused-opt    | 86%
0.4     | launch_wait| cuda-queue   | 94%  <-- queuing
```
Devon: The `kv_miss` fallback invokes kernels we haven't prioritized in the selector, and large microbatches make those misses amplify queuing.
Irene: So two levers: kernel selector needs the quantized/fast variant for the miss path, and batching heuristics shouldn't coalesce fallback requests into big microbatches.
AJ: Agreed. We've historically seen max_batch_size increases reduce avg cost but worsen tails when stragglers appear.
Sneh: Suggestion: if route reports recent KV miss rate > 10%, temporarily shrink coalesce window and lower max_coalesce_batch. Also mark those requests as "do-not-coalesce" where possible.
Liam: Another idea: speculative prefetch for likely keys during request parse so miss probability drops. Tradeoff is extra reads and slightly higher avg GPU memory traffic.
Devon: We tried a prefetch experiment in dev. p99 improved ~20%, but throughput/efficiency worsened ~3% due to extra kv reads.
AJ: Need SLO math. Target for this route: p99 < 250ms. During the spike p99 hit ~720ms. That's a hard fail for canary.
Irene: Simulation shows that limiting utilization to ~78% reduces queueing and tails in this profile. But throughput and revenue take a hit. Do we accept lower util for better SLOs?
Sneh: Ops-bot indicated queueing grows nonlinearly past 85% util. Once queuing dominates, kernel improvements have marginal effect.
Devon: Action items I propose:
- Short: patch kernel selector to prefer a quantized fallback variant and add a `kv-miss` hint so batching shrinks for that request class.
- Mid: implement a runtime policy that watches `recent_util`, `kv_miss_rate`, and `p99` to toggle conservative batching and admission thresholds or route to lighter model variants.
AJ: Also add a canary guardrail: fail the deploy if canary p99 > 2x baseline or >250ms absolute.
Liam: For the selector change add a unit test that simulates a `kv_miss` and asserts kernel priority and batch assignment; include a perf microtest that asserts p99 behavior under synthetic cold-kv workload.
Devon: I'll open a small PR today with: selector priority change, batching hint addition, and a `--kv-prefetch` flag for dev canaries.
Sneh: For rollout, recommend staged ramp with synthetic tail tests: long contexts and cold-heavy KV pattern, watch p50/p95/p99 separately.
Devon: Data point: dialing fallback microbatch size down to 2 reduced p99 by a lot but cut throughput ~12%. Might be worth a schedule-based policy (peaks only).
AJ: That suggests a capacity playbook: when util > 80% AND p99 > SLO, flip to conservative coalescing and enable shedding for low-priority traffic.
Liam: We should codify the policy as: if (recent_util > U_threshold OR kv_miss_rate > M_threshold) AND p99 > SLO then set batch_coalesce_window = small, admission_cutoff = stricter, enable fallback-prefetch = false/true depending on cost model.
Devon: I'll include a pseudo-config in the PR description. Also will add instrumentation to surface `kv_miss_rate` per route in the Console.
Irene: I'll take ownership of the canary alert rule and the deploy halt criteria. Devon, you + Liam own the selector+policy work. AJ will own the regression alert.
CI-bot: quick smoke passed for dev branch.
Ops-bot: alert: gpu-queue-mdx reported short spikes at 03:12 UTC (8 instances).
Devon: noted, I'll correlate those timestamps with the new traces.
Irene: Closing the loop: target is p99 < 250ms while keeping utilization >= ~75% generally. Playbook: temporary util caps, conservative batching, shedding rules, and fallback-prefetch optional.
Devon: PR incoming in ~2 hours; ping me if you want an early review. (reacts :rocket:)
